title: Set aside (different measures): Triglycerides and coronary heart disease: a raised risk, or no link once other risk factors are accounted for?
explanation: Claim A reports a significant increase in coronary heart disease risk associated with higher triglyceride levels, whereas Claim B finds no significant association after adjusting for conventional risk factors.
a_text: A meta-analysis of 29 studies shows an adjusted odds ratio for coronary heart disease of 1.72 (95% CI, 1.56 to 1.90) comparing individuals in the top third with those in the bottom third of usual log-triglyceride values.
b_text: Triglyceride level is not significantly associated with coronary heart disease risk after adjustment for conventional risk factors (HR 0.99 per 1-SD higher value).

supporting_papers.title: Triglycerides and the Risk of Coronary Heart Disease
Major Lipids, Apolipoproteins, and Risk of Vascular Disease

audit.reason: Different adjustment and contrast: Sarwar 2006's own conclusion says its triglyceride–heart-disease link depends heavily on other risk factors and leaves any independent link open, while the 2009 pooled analysis reports the per-standard-deviation estimate alongside the other blood lipids, so both statements can be true.
